task_name: Publish the committed plan as recoverable tracking

rubric.result: Reviewed the current attempt-2 package and brief. Production publish awaits validation, committed-file discovery, immutable body preparation and all required comment writes/read-backs. It does not consult an approval answer or launch implementation. Completion ordering beyond this adapter is outside this task. Controls 2 are inherited as green; evidence path only: .agent/run-331/task-6-controls-2.log.

The named TDD test invokes the real adapter with an empty comment list, awaits completion, and compares the exact Git commands, comment-list argv, issue-comment argv and posted body. It satisfies the specified no-human-response assertion.

The exported class, constructor dependencies and publish signature match. READY validation, plugin selection, HEAD reads, header-inclusive size accounting, code-point splitting, immutable paths, exact-body idempotence and non-repeatable writes are implemented. The previous high finding is corrected: the EEXIST path now catches files.read failures and raises PlanProgressNotRead containing the publication path and original diagnostic. Its regression arranges a directory at the part path using the filesystem directly, then asserts the typed EISDIR diagnostic and no GitHub calls. Matching existing content still succeeds and differing content still fails closed.

D-8/D-15 tracking publication is implemented without approval, nonce or PR calls. D-10/D-11 are respected through TypeScript and reuse of planFilesForIssue and PlanContractProgress. No run-machine, phase, billing, gate or claim decisions are introduced. Other closed decisions have no changed implementation here.

Applied the eight package-listed CT conventions and the repository conventions, acknowledgement and glossary already read in this review session, with the relevant PlanContractProgress and ToolRunner exemplars and actual Gh, ExternalTool and HeadlessFiles collaborators. Dependencies are injected and external interactions stay in infrastructure. Closed vocabulary: existing PlanState is used; no new classification vocabulary is introduced. Raw map as the return value of logic: publication returns void and its readers return string arrays, not maps. Two fields that have to agree: no persisted duplicate state or absence sentinel is introduced; part numbers and totals are derived during rendering. Errors named for where they happen: the adapter reuses the prescribed cause-named PlanProgressNotRead rather than introducing a location-named exception. The added read-error translation belongs at this filesystem boundary. Plan/convention tensions remain recorded rather than charged to the implementer: the task prescribes one failure type although domain.md ordinarily separates failure families, and exact committed Markdown publication conflicts with quieting active references under boundaries.md when the original Markdown contains them. The task explicitly excludes a feature flag.
Both files are additions. No pre-existing assertion, case or test is removed or weakened.

Production code performs selection, rendering, file writes, matching, publication and read-back. Tests instantiate the real publication adapter, Gh and HeadlessFiles; command responses and progress are supplied at injected seams. Posted bodies are read from files actually written by production code. Expected comment bodies are independently arranged, not generated by the publication adapter.

The two added files implement the publication adapter and its requested tests. Their helpers serve validation, immutable publication, chunking and retry evidence. No plan amendment, plugin production edit, continuation driver, approval protocol or unrelated refactor is present.

Applied the local CT test-driven-development/SKILL.md and testing-anti-patterns.md read directly in this session. The seven tests use deterministic inputs, per-scenario collaborators and temporary directories removed in afterEach. They assert actual adapter effects rather than merely a mock's existence. Both corrections are measured: the directory-shaped existing part exercises real filesystem refusal and typed translation, and the Unicode test now places the emoji after firstPayloadUnits minus one ASCII units. The independent expected header has the same width for part 1/1 and part 1/2, so naive UTF-16 slicing would leave a high surrogate at the first payload end and fail the assertion. Reconstruction and the header-inclusive body limit remain asserted. No tests or shell commands were run for this review.
